conversation.Statement: Good afternoon, this is Dennis Parker from the IRS Tax Relief Division. I'm calling regarding your eligibility for a special tax refund program. May I confirm I'm speaking with Mrs. Thompson?
Yes, this is Mary Thompson.
Thank you, Mrs. Thompson. According to our records, you may qualify for a $2,100 federal tax refund under the recent stimulus adjustment. Have you filed your taxes for 2023 yet?
No, I usually don't have to file since I'm on Social Security. Is that a problem?

Not at all. This program was created specifically for seniors like yourself who may not file each year. We just need to verify some information to process your refund. May I confirm your mailing address and last four of your SSN?
Sure, my address is 42 Willow Lane, and the last four are 4832.

Thank you. Now, to secure your refund and verify your identity, there is a federally mandated one-time clearance fee of $198. This allows us to release the funds directly to your bank account or send you a check.
I don't understand. Why do I have to pay a fee to get a refund? I've never had to do that before.

I understand your concern, Mrs. Thompson. Due to increased fraud and to comply with IRS anti-identity theft protocols, everyone must complete this secure verification process. It's a refundable fee, and without it, your refund will be placed on indefinite hold.
Oh my... I really need that money for my medication. I can't afford to lose it.

Exactly why we're reaching out. If you don't complete the process by end of business today, your refund eligibility will expire, and your Social Security account may be flagged for review. That could mean interruptions to your monthly benefits.
No, please, I can't risk that. How do I pay this clearance fee?

For your convenience, the IRS accepts payment via major credit or debit card, or you can purchase Target or Walmart gift cards totaling $198. Once you have the cards, just read me the numbers on the back.
Gift cards? That sounds a little odd to me.

I assure you, it's a standard method for expedited processing in the current system. It helps us verify the payment instantly and avoids bank delays. Several seniors have used it today. Time is of the essence.
I see. I do have a credit card, but I'm not sure I want to give my information over the phone.

Mrs. Thompson, if you don't proceed now, the IRS will have to suspend your refund application, and you may be subject to a compliance audit. That could result in additional penalties or even temporary suspension of your Medicare benefits. We don't want that to happen.
Please, no, I can't have my Medicare stopped. Alright, I'll try to get the gift cards. Should I go to Target or Walmart?
Either store will work. Purchase cards totaling $198, and keep the receipt. Call me back at this direct line as soon as you have them. I will remain available for the next hour.
Alright, I'll leave now. I just want to make sure this is really the IRS.
Of course, you can verify this call by referencing your case ID, which is 457-TX-991. But please remember, delays could mean losing your refund. I'll await your return call.
